newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: BTNZ sees NZ dlr down by June, set to rise again.
newsitem.headline: BTNZ sees NZ dlr down by June, set to rise again.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar will weaken over the first half of 1997, but will regain lost ground over the second half as the Reserve Bank of New Zealand swings back into tightening mode, Bankers Trust New Zealand said on Thursday.
BTNZ said its outlook for the currency meant the fundamental overvaluation it thought existed would persist for some time.
In the first half of the year, BTNZ said, short term interest rate differentials would narrow as the U.S. economy gathered pace and New Zealand data maintained a softish tone.
Nevertheless, BTNZ expected the fall in the Kiwi to be moderate and short-lived.
Fiscal stimulus from mid-1998, and above-trend economic growth from the middle of 1997, would prompt the RBNZ into action.

"At this stage, we think a significant correction in the currency is more likely to occur in 1998 than 1997 -- being mindful, however, that currency movements tend to be larger than expected," BTNZ said.
Its view was driven by the present easing bias of the RBNZ.
"While this is expected to push the NZ dollar lower, we could get a different mix of easier conditions," BTNZ said.
"On the upside, the risk is that the RBNZ moves into tightening mode earlier than we think. If this occurs, then the downside for the TWI (Trade-Weighted Index) is very limited.
"All told, our view is for the TWI to soften to 66 by June, before rising to 67 by December (partway to a peak of 70 by mid-1998)."
